# hatsu_ino

> Arduino-based JDM car melody box that plays a WAV audio file through a speaker when the car's ignition turns on, then sleeps until the next start.

hatsu_ino ("hatsu" = first sound, "ino" = Arduino) is an open-source (MIT licensed) hardware + firmware project. An Arduino Nano reads WAV files from an SD card and plays them through a PAM8403 amplifier and speaker on ignition power-up, then enters deep sleep (~0.1µA) until the next power cycle. Each board revision is self-contained under `boards/<version>/` in the source repo, with its own wiring guide, Arduino sketch, a pure-logic header (`logic.h`) with no hardware dependency, and a native Catch2 test suite covering that logic.

## Docs

- [Home](https://arturvrsampaio.github.io/hatsu_ino/): project overview and board list
- [v0 board guide](https://arturvrsampaio.github.io/hatsu_ino/boards/v0/): components, full wiring instructions (power, SD card SPI, audio path including the RC low-pass filter), CONFIG.TXT key reference, WAV file requirements, error/troubleshooting codes, and testing instructions for the first production board (Arduino Nano + PAM8403)

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ArturVRSampaio/hatsu_ino): firmware source, native test suite, CI workflows
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/ArturVRSampaio/hatsu_ino/blob/master/LICENSE): MIT
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/ArturVRSampaio/hatsu_ino/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add a board variant, fix a bug, or improve the docs
